purpose: Prototype v6k: KeepCount's procedure (stages, the two counts, the comparators, the positive control and the smallest difference) applied to summaries that writing-process research reports, instead of the tile transform with v4's external scale. Asked for by the pre-review of the outline for the Journal of Writing Research (round 1, point A: the example summary is not one used in writing research) and decided by the researcher (decision 5 of .steering/20261108-paper-a-jowr-reframe; decisions 1-3 of .steering/20261108-v6k-standard-summaries). Three summaries: (U) the sentence summary of v6 without the external scale (per sentence the share of time in gaps at or above a threshold and the log of the median gap below it); (B) P-bursts as defined in Table 5 of the KLiCKe paper (mean length, and their spread); (I) the pause means of the same table (gaps over 200 ms: all, within words, between words). Each at fixed thresholds of 2 s, 1 s and 500 ms, and at a threshold per writer from a mixture of lognormals in the manner of Baaijen et al. (2012).
fixed_before_running: Written on 2026-11-08 after seeing the records of v6 to v6j (results/prototype_v6*/) and the pre-review of the outline (round 1). No value of U, B, I or of a writer's threshold has been computed for any person of any dataset, and the persons drawn here have not been looked at by any earlier version (KUPA from position 437 of v6's draw order, LWP from position 204 of v6e's). A first draft was sent to Codex (codex-consult, the conditions text only, no data; .steering/20261108-v6k-standard-summaries/codex-consult-output.md) and changed after its seven points (decision 4 of that folder): the rule splits cells that cannot change by construction from those that can and names undecided cells apart from mixed directions; the positive control R is counted on the same persons as the stage it gates; the invariances are stated only at fixed thresholds, and a writer's threshold held at the text's value is added beside the refitted one; the mixture's undefined cases, several starts and diagnostics are fixed; bursts cut by a part's edges are reported and a spread over complete bursts is added beside the rule; the KLiCKe measures are named proxies built from press times, with a table of what differs; paired differences in count 2 are recomputed on the persons common to both stages; limits extended.
status: The summaries, rows, comparators and rules are fixed here before any value of them is seen, and counted on persons not used before: a confirmation in this sense (status c) for the rule of part 1 and a description for the rest. The procedure itself and the rows were chosen on earlier persons (v6-v6e).

sources.klicke_table5: Tian, Crossley & Van Waes (2025), The KLiCKe corpus, Journal of Writing Research 17(1), doi:10.17239/jowr-2025.17.01.02, Table 5 (p. 43; the PDF from jowr.org, SHA-256 48fb8d6667e53257306716766ca0cf8f28639988dafa8ccc17b15cbbf638c732), verbatim: 'mean length of P-bursts: The mean length of the string of actions delineated by an initial and end pause exceeding 2 seconds and is measured in characters'; 'mean length of pauses: The mean length of latencies between the previous and the current action that exceed 200ms in text production and is measured in seconds'; 'mean length of within-word pauses: The mean length of latencies within words that exceed 200ms'; 'mean length of between-word pauses: The mean length of latencies between words that exceed 200ms'. The same paper (p. 26-27): 'burst lengths and variations have been reported to show predictive power of essay quality'.
sources.baaijen_2012: Baaijen, Galbraith & de Glopper (2012), Keystroke analysis, Written Communication 29(3) (the publisher's PDF from the University of Groningen repository, SHA-256 822d49ea07af8bd191252f3393a2defbeecc79fef8b1807e8d2e6be1c5da9aa6): mixtures fitted per participant to log between-word pauses and chosen by BIC (p. 262-264); for the example participant 'the more extreme pauses should be treated as a miscellaneous group identified by a threshold determined by the tail of the second lognormal distribution. In this case, three standard deviations above the mean' (p. 263); 'thresholds can be established relative to the particular characteristics of individual writers rather than against a general criterion' (p. 269-270). Three components fitted best for 58% of participants and two for 19% (p. 264).
sources.van_waes_2021: 2 s as a common fixed threshold, sometimes 500 ms ([13] of references.md, verbatim in decisions record 1 of .steering/20261108-paper-a-jowr-reframe).

data: KUPA-KEYS TASK-1 (copy) and TASK-2 (essay) as v6's conditions (files and SHA-256 there); LWP as v6e's conditions (file, SHA-256, counted presses and kinds there). Aalto 136M is not used (decision 6 of .steering/20261108-paper-a-jowr-reframe: it moves to an appendix reference). Kinds as v6b's kind_b (KUPA) and v6e's (LWP); sentence and word starts and the gap labels (sentence, subsentence, word, within, other) as v6b.labels.

participants.kupa: the ids of TASK-2 sorted, in v6's draw order (v6.draw_order(..., 0)); positions 0-436 were looked at by v6 and v6b and are skipped; from position 437 on, the first 200 ids eligible under v6b's rule (both tasks: at least 5 sentences, at least 5 full 10 s windows, every sentence holds a gap under before, after and none). The run checks that positions 0-436 give exactly v6's and v6b's persons (their SHA-256) and that the new persons overlap neither.
participants.lwp: the ids of train_logs.csv in v6e's draw order (v6.draw_order(..., 2)); positions 0-203 were looked at by v6e and are skipped (checked as above against v6e's SHA-256); from position 204 on, the first 200 ids eligible under v6e's rule.
participants.count_1_persons: per dataset and task, persons with at least 8 sentences and at least one held gap in every part under both baselines (v6b); the numbers left out are recorded.
participants.count_2_persons: the 200 KUPA persons, for every stage whose vector exists in both tasks; a person without a vector at a stage (defined below) is left out of that stage in both sets, and n is recorded per stage (rank rates depend on n).

units: sentences only (cut at the sentence-end keys; the gap before a sentence counted in it, counting 'before', for every stage unless a row says otherwise). 10 s windows are not counted. A part is a set of sentences: odd/even or halves (v6b.parts).

thresholds.fixed: theta = 2000 ms (main), 1000 ms and 500 ms. A gap g is long at theta if g >= theta - 1e-6 ms (src/keystroke TOL_MS, as v6), short otherwise. Index in keys: 2000 0, 1000 1, 500 2, writer 3, writer_fixed 4 (0 for stages without a threshold).

writer.fit: per record (a person's series in one task, or an operated series; so the estimate belongs to a writer in a task, not to a writer), a one-dimensional Gaussian mixture fitted to ln of the gaps labelled 'word' (the gap before the first letter of a word that follows a space; v6b.labels), all of them, with no lower cut (gaps are positive by v6.clean). k = 1 is fitted in closed form (mean and standard deviation, ddof 0) whenever the record holds at least 2 such gaps; k = 2 and 3 are fitted by EM only if the record holds at least 20k such gaps. EM starts: (i) means at the quantiles (2i + 1) / (2k) of the data, each standard deviation the data's divided by k, equal weights; (ii-v) four starts with means at k data points drawn without replacement by numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 92, dataset, task, place, row index, k, start]), standard deviations and weights as (i). Each start iterates until the log-likelihood rises by less than 1e-10 or for 2000 iterations; a standard deviation is floored at 0.01 (ln units) after each step. A start whose log-likelihood is not finite, or whose fitted components include one with weight below 0.02, is discarded; of the rest the highest log-likelihood is kept (the earliest start on a tie). A k with no start kept is not considered. The k with the lowest BIC (3k - 1 parameters, n the number of gaps) is chosen; BICs within 1e-9 count as a tie and the smaller k is taken.
writer.threshold: components of the chosen fit ordered by mean; theta_w = exp(mu_j + 3 sigma_j) ms with j the second component if k >= 2 and the first if k = 1 (Baaijen's example: the tail of the second lognormal, three standard deviations above its mean; with three components the third is the 'miscellaneous' long group).
writer.use: theta_w replaces theta in U, B and Bsd, in two forms. writer (main of the two): in count 1 the text's theta_w is used for both parts of the text, and every operated series gets its own theta_w fitted on its own gaps (the summary is a function of the record it is given). writer_fixed (count 1 only): the text's theta_w is kept for every operated series, so that a change at writer_fixed comes from where the gaps fall and a difference between writer and writer_fixed from the threshold's adaptation. A record with fewer than 2 'word' gaps has no theta_w and is left out at both (counted).
writer.reported: per dataset and task, over persons: five-number summaries of theta_w, of the weight of component j and of the gaps fitted; the frequencies of the chosen k; the numbers of starts discarded and of starts that reached 2000 iterations; and, in count 1, the five-number summary over persons of |ln theta_w(row) - ln theta_w(text)| for each row.

stages.S0: v6's: quantiles 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95 of ln gap over the gaps held by the part (comparator: the stage of times).
stages.S1: v6's: median and IQR over the part's sentences of p and q with v4's external scale, at 2 s (comparator: the transform of the manuscript).
stages.U: per sentence (its held gaps), u_rest = share of the sentence's time in long gaps (sum of long gaps over sum of all gaps) and u_speed = ln of the median of its short gaps (ms). The part's vector: median and IQR over its sentences of u_speed and of u_rest (4 numbers). A sentence with no short gap has no u_speed and is left out of u_speed's median and IQR only; a part with no u_speed has no vector. Counted at each threshold (U_2000, U_1000, U_500, U_writer).
stages.B: the part's held gaps in index order, split into runs of consecutive indices (a part under odd/even holds several runs). In a run, a P-burst is the stretch of presses between two long gaps, or between a run's end and a long gap; its length is the number of presses in it (1 + its short gaps). The part's value: the mean length over its bursts (KLiCKe's 'mean length of P-bursts', with counted presses as 'characters'). 1 number. At each threshold. Reported per part: the share of bursts cut by a run's edge rather than bounded by long gaps at both ends (five-number summary over persons).
stages.Bsd: the standard deviation (ddof 0) of the same burst lengths (a part with one burst: 0). 1 number. At each threshold.
stages.I: KLiCKe's three pause means over the gaps held by the part, in seconds: all gaps > 200 ms; gaps labelled 'within' > 200 ms; gaps labelled 'word' > 200 ms (strictly greater, as 'exceed'). 3 numbers. A part with no gap > 200 ms in one of the three has no vector. Not counted at the thresholds (200 ms is KLiCKe's).
stages.R: v6b's LOC (median ln gap at sentence, subsentence, word and within-word starts; sentence minus within; the share of long time at sentence and subsentence starts at 2 s; lag-1 correlation of ln gaps): the reference observable and the positive control of count 1, as v6b and v6e. Not in count 2 under the rule (reported).
stages.by_construction: stated before running and checked in the run at the fixed thresholds only (a violation stops it; at writer the threshold can move with the record, at writer_fixed it is the text's and the statements hold there too): (a) B depends only on the numbers of gaps, of long gaps and of runs in the part: with r runs, G gaps and L long gaps it is (G + r) / (L + r); an operation that keeps each run's multiset of gaps leaves it unchanged. So B's change is 0 under inside/before (both baselines) and under shuffled_in_halves/before under halves. (b) I's first number depends only on the part's multiset. (c) U's change is 0 under inside/before (each sentence keeps its multiset), as S1's (v6e). A change of 0 against a base above 0 gives a share of 0; against a base of 0, 1/2 (v6b's ties); both are reported.
stages.Bsd_complete: the standard deviation (ddof 0) of the lengths of the bursts bounded by long gaps at both ends (KLiCKe's 'initial and end pause'); a part with fewer than 2 such bursts has no value. At 2 s only; reported beside the rule (it removes the edges that odd/even parts cut).
stages.proxies: U, B, Bsd and I are proxies built from press times, not Inputlog's measures. What differs from KLiCKe's Table 5: (1) actions and characters: here counted presses (letters, digits, space, Enter, punctuation, Backspace, Delete; LWP masks letters and digits as q); a deletion, a paste, an IME confirmation or a held key is one press or several presses here, while a character count differs; (2) events not counted (modifiers, arrows, mouse, LWP's non-production events) are not presses, so a gap spans them and cannot be told from a pause; (3) KLiCKe cut inactive periods at the start and end; not done here; (4) bursts cut by a part's or record's edge are counted (KLiCKe's bursts have pauses at both ends; Bsd_complete keeps only those); (5) long is >= theta here, 'exceeding' (>) in KLiCKe; (6) word and within-word are v6b's labels from the kinds of keys, not Inputlog's text analysis.
stages.dimensions: the stages differ in dimension (S0 7, S1 4, U 4, R 7, I 3, B 1, Bsd 1); distances are Euclidean on scaled features, so a stage of more numbers is not made comparable to one of fewer.

rows.operations: as v6's KUPA sentence rows, applied to both datasets: text/after, text/none (countings), inside/before, shuffled/before, shuffled_in_halves/before, with v6.make_rows' operations and keys (dataset code KUPA 0, LWP 2; task copy 0, essay 1, LWP 0; place = the index of the id in the sorted ids, as v6 and v6e). Only the press times are rebuilt; kinds, starts and labels stay with the presses.
rows.control_row: random_half (v6j's): rests at 2 s of the sentences outside a uniform random half moved into that half by v6f's swap, keys [20261031, 6, 32 | 33, dataset, task, place, 2] as v6j. Reported beside the rule: a concentration of long gaps in particular sentences, which U should show if it can show anything of where the long gaps fall.

count_1.how: v6b.one() per dataset, task, baseline (odd/even, halves), row, stage and threshold: share of persons whose change (mean over the two parts of the distance between the operated and the text vector, features scaled by the standard deviation over persons and parts of the text) exceeds the distance between their own two parts (ties 1/2), with a 95% percentile interval over 2000 bootstrap resamples of persons; the same share against the median distance to another person; medians of change and base and their ratio; zero bases.
count_1.persons_per_stage: a stage is counted on the persons with a vector for the text and the row in both parts; the numbers left out are recorded. For R as v6b (text/none has no R by construction). For part 1's rule, each stage and its gate R are counted again on the persons who have both (rule persons), so that the gate and the stage share persons; the numbers left out of the rule persons are recorded per cell.
count_1.keys: bootstrap numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 90, dataset, task, stage, row index, baseline, threshold, gate]) with stage S0 0, S1 1, U 2, B 3, Bsd 4, I 5, R 6, Bsd_complete 7; row index as v6 (text/after 1, text/none 2, inside 3, shuffled 4, shuffled_in_halves 5, random_half 6); baseline odd/even 0, halves 1; threshold as thresholds.fixed; gate 0 for the counts on all persons of a stage, and for the rule persons of stage X, 1 + X's stage index (R's count there uses the same gate value with stage 6).

count_2.how: KUPA copy -> essay and essay -> copy on the 200 persons, at every stage and threshold: v6.standardise under 'main' and 'registration_scale', Euclidean distance, rank_auc (per-person rank of the genuine among 199 impostors, ties 1/2) with a 95% interval over 2000 bootstrap resamples, top1, Rank-1/5/10/20 with intervals (v6c.rank_rates), EER (v6c.eer). Reading as v6: detectable if the lower end of rank_auc is above 0.5; size against 0.60.
count_2.paired: x - y on the persons who have both stages in both tasks (common persons): both stages standardised, ranked and resampled again on those persons, with the resamples of y; n recorded. Pairs: U_2000 - S1, B - S1, I - S1, S0 - U_2000; U_theta - U_2000 for theta 1000, 500 and writer.
count_2.keys: bootstrap numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 91, direction, stage, scale, threshold, paired]) with direction copy -> essay 0, essay -> copy 1; stage and threshold as count 1; scale main 0, registration 1; paired 0 for a stage's own count, and for a pair 1 + the pair's index in the list above.
count_2.stages: S0, S1, U, B, Bsd and I at every threshold that applies (writer only: writer_fixed is count 1's); R reported, not in the paired list.

checks.reuse: before the new persons are counted, the code that rebuilds the rows and the vectors is run on earlier persons and must equal the earlier records, or the run stops: on v6's 200 KUPA persons, count 2 of S0 and S1 in sentences under 'main' (rank_auc within 1e-12 of v6's record); on v6b's persons, count 1 of KUPA essay in sentences, both baselines, every row, stages S0, S1 and R (share_vs_own and its interval equal to v6b's record); on v6e's persons, count 1 of LWP in sentences, both baselines, rows inside, shuffled and shuffled_in_halves, stages S1 and R (equal to v6e's record). These check the reuse of code, not its validity.
checks.construction: the identities of stages.by_construction are checked per person (|change| <= 1e-9 where the change must be 0).

rule.part_1_pause_location: fixed before running. Main cells: KUPA essay and LWP; sentences; odd/even and halves; rows inside/before, shuffled/before and shuffled_in_halves/before; threshold 2 s: 12 cells per stage, counted on the rule persons (count_1.persons_per_stage). A cell is evaluable for a stage only if R reads the row above 0.60 there (the positive control: the operation is seen by the reference on the same persons and parts); otherwise it is 'control not met' and not read. Cells where the stage's change is 0 by construction (stages.by_construction: U inside 4 cells; B inside 4 and shuffled_in_halves under halves 2) are 'fixed by construction': reported, named and not read. The label of each of U, B, Bsd and I is given over its evaluable cells that can change: 'shows these operations beyond the smallest difference' if every one reads above 0.60; 'does not show them beyond it' if every one reads below 0.60; 'not beyond, partly undecided' if none reads above and at least one below; 'beyond, partly undecided' if none reads below and at least one above; 'undecided' if every one is undecided; 'mixed directions' if at least one reads above and one below. Fewer than 4 such cells: 'not evaluable'. Reported beside the label: the number of cells by dataset and row in each class, the cells fixed by construction, the cells where the control is not met, and the persons left out.
rule.part_2_thresholds: descriptive. For U, B and Bsd, in the 12 main cells: the reading class (above, below, undecided against 0.60) at 1 s, 500 ms, writer and writer_fixed, and the number of cells whose class equals that at 2 s (the cells are correlated; agreements are not independent replications).
rule.part_3_writer: descriptive. Per stage and threshold, KUPA both directions, both scales: rank_auc with interval and its two readings; the paired differences.
rule.wording: a share is the share of persons whose change exceeds their own variation, not an effect size; below 0.60 is 'not beyond the smallest difference', not 'absent'. An interval that crosses 0.60 is 'undecided'.

prediction: Claude's, written before running. P1: R reads shuffled and shuffled_in_halves above 0.60 in all 8 of their main cells (as v6b and v6e). P2: U_2000 does not read any shuffle cell above 0.60 (label 'does not show them beyond it' or 'not beyond, partly undecided'). P3: B is labelled 'does not show them beyond it' (its 6 changeable cells below 0.60). P4: Bsd reads both shuffles above 0.60 in at least 4 of their 8 main cells (the spread of burst lengths depends on how long gaps cluster in order). P5: I reads inside above 0.60 in at least 3 of its 4 main cells and both shuffles above 0.60 in all 8 (its word and within-word means move when gaps change places across labels). P6: in KUPA copy -> essay under 'main', U_2000's rank_auc exceeds S1's (paired difference on common persons, lower end above 0); a difference does not identify its source (the scale, the log and the definitions all differ). P7: the median theta_w over KUPA essay persons lies between 500 and 2000 ms. P8: for each of U, B and Bsd, the reading class at 1 s and 500 ms equals that at 2 s in at least 8 of the 12 main cells. No value of v6k had been seen.
main_cells: fixed before running, shown first: part 1's rule with its 12 cells per stage (U_2000, B, Bsd, I), R on the rule persons, and Bsd_complete beside it; then count 2 of KUPA copy -> essay under 'main' at S0, S1, U_2000, B, Bsd, I and the paired differences; then the thresholds (including writer_fixed); then the rest in the order of this file.

record.public: results/prototype_v6k/record.json: counts and summaries over persons and the provenance; no press time, gap, key, text, per-person vector, per-person value, per-person threshold or id (ids only as the SHA-256 of their sorted list). The data are not redistributed.
record.provenance: git commit and dirty state of the conditions, code and lock; SHA-256 of the conditions, the earlier conditions and records, the code and the data; versions.

limits_written_before: Counted presses stand for KLiCKe's 'actions' and 'characters' (modifiers, arrows and mouse events are not counted; KUPA drops key repeats, LWP cannot); KLiCKe's measures come from Inputlog on .idfx files after cutting inactive periods at the start and end, which is not done here, so the values are not Inputlog's values. The burst ends at a long gap only (P-burst), not at a revision (R-burst). A long gap is >= theta, KLiCKe's 'exceeding' is >; they differ only at gaps of exactly theta. The writer's threshold follows Baaijen's example for between-word pauses with a rule fixed here for the number of components and for which tail is used; Baaijen fitted per location and found single lognormals at sentence and subsentence boundaries, and mixtures are not fitted per location here. Refitting theta_w on an operated series makes the threshold move with the operation; a threshold fixed per writer from other material would answer a different question. Sentence summaries of revised text: sentences are cut at the sentence-end keys in the order typed, so a sentence mixes drafting and revision presses, and the parts mix phases of the session. The parts are fixed (odd/even, halves), not random splits. Many correlated cells; only part 1 has a rule. Status c only for part 1, on new persons, with a procedure chosen on earlier persons. A share shows sensitivity of a summary to an operation on press times; it says nothing about the cognitive meaning of a pause or the quality of a text. Bsd responds to order but does not tell apart every reordering (a reversal or a swap of equal lengths leaves it). The writer's threshold can jump when the chosen k changes; the jumps are part of the summary as defined.
rerun_rule: if a defect of the code is found after the first run, the first record is kept unchanged, the fix and the reason are committed, and the rerun is reported separately beside the first; the conditions are not changed after the first run except by such a recorded amendment.
